name: Builder
intent: Construct a complex object step by step, so the same process can build different results and the call reads clearly.
scenario: A pizza shop builds pizzas with a size, crust, optional extra sauce and any toppings. A menu offers ready-made recipes like Margherita.
problem: Pizza has many parts, most optional. A constructor with six positional arguments is unreadable (true, false, true...) and every new option adds another parameter or another constructor overload.
solution: Move construction into a Builder with one named method per part and a build() at the end. Callers set only what they need, in readable steps. build() validates and returns the finished object. A Director can store common recipes.
pain: new Pizza("large", "thin", true, ["ham"], false) is hard to read
Callers must pass every argument, even defaults
Adding an option changes every call site
Nothing validates the combination before the object exists
benefits: Named steps make each call self-explanatory
Defaults live in the builder; callers set only what differs
A new option is one new builder method
build() is a single place to validate
whenToUse: Objects with many optional parameters or configuration steps
The same construction process must produce different representations
You want immutable results assembled in stages: HTTP requests, queries, documents
whenNotToUse: Objects with two or three simple fields: a constructor is clearer
Your language already has named and optional parameters that solve the problem
The extra builder class would be the largest part of the code
pitfalls: Forgetting to call build() and passing the half-built builder around
Reusing one builder for two objects without resetting it
Required fields that are only checked at runtime, not by the compiler
Boilerplate: the builder mirrors the product's fields

roles.label: Director
roles.description: Knows common recipes and drives a builder through them.

roles.label: Builder
roles.description: Offers a step per part and a build() method.

quiz.question: A function builds a report with `new Report(title, true, false, true, 12, null, false)`. Last week two boolean values were swapped and a wrong footer shipped. The language has no named arguments. What is the best fix?
options: Add overloads for the six most common argument combinations, so most calls need fewer values
Add a ReportBuilder with named steps such as withFooter() and withPageSize(), ending in a build() call
Write a comment above each call explaining the order of the arguments in the constructor
Change the booleans to strings such as "yes" and "no", so a swapped pair is easier to spot
quiz.explanation: Named steps make each setting readable at the call site and let callers skip defaults. Overloads multiply with every option, and comments or strings still leave the positions easy to swap.

quiz.question: A shared PizzaBuilder instance makes a Margherita, then is used again for a Hawaiian. The Hawaiian comes out with Margherita's basil as well. What is the cause and the fix?
options: The pizza keeps a reference to the builder, so make build() return a deep copy of the builder
The builder should be a singleton, so all pizzas are built from the same recipe state
Builder state survives build(), so make a new builder for each pizza
build() ran twice, so guard it with a flag that allows only one call per builder
quiz.explanation: A builder keeps state between steps, so reusing it carries old toppings into the next product. A new builder or a reset in build() separates the products. A singleton makes the sharing worse.

quiz.question: An HttpRequest builder has optional methods for headers, body and timeout, and also url(), which is required. A caller forgot url() and the NullPointer appeared deep in the sender, three layers later. What is the most robust change?
options: Document that url() must be called, and add the rule to the checklist
Check for a missing url at the start of send(), where the failure used to show
Default the url to localhost, so build() always returns a sendable request
Take the url at builder creation, and let build() check the rest
quiz.explanation: Required data belongs in the builder's creation, and build() is the single place to reject an invalid combination before the object exists. A check in send() fails too late, and a silent default sends requests to the wrong place.
